description.narrative: The KTP will develop and roll out ColdHub pre-coolers (CHPC), which will incorporate a hybrid solar-powered pre-cooling storage system using a different refrigeration system based on vapour compression-absorption and advanced numerical modelling to optimise sizing of the solar PV panels. The CHPCs will be located in smallholder farmers clusters to reduce the temperature of produce from typically 27°C to 12 - 15°C close to the producer before transfer to the ColdHubs, where the temperature is reduced to 8 - 10°C for optimal storage. This will; a. Protect the quality (and value) of the produce by reducing spoilage in transit b. Avoid overloading of the cold rooms, where the excess heat in the produce puts strain on the compressor based refrigeration in cooling from 27°C to 8 - 10°C c. Extend produce shelf life from 2 to 21 days

To develop a hybrid solar-powered off-grid pre-cooling storage system for smallholder farmers clusters in Nigeria to supplement existing cold rooms, minimize agro-food waste, improve cooling efficiency, increase farmers' income and drive business growth in ColdHubs. Innovation area – Storage The KTP will develop and roll out ColdHub pre-coolers (CHPC), which will incorporate a hybrid solar-powered pre-cooling storage system using a different refrigeration system based on vapour compression-absorption and advanced numerical modelling to optimise sizing of the solar PV panels. The CHPCs will be located in smallholder farmers clusters to reduce the temperature of produce from typically 27°C to 12 - 15°C close to the producer before transfer to the ColdHubs, where the temperature is reduced to 8 - 10°C for optimal storage. This will; a. Protect the quality (and value) of the produce by reducing spoilage in transit b. Avoid overloading of the cold rooms, where the excess heat in the produce puts strain on the compressor based refrigeration in cooling from 27°C to 8 - 10°C c. Extend produce shelf life from 2 to 21 days ODA – the CHPCs will have an immediate impact on the income of smallholders in Nigeria by increasing the quantity of produce that reaches the markets / wholesalers due to the increased shelf life. ColdHubs project an increase in income from $60 to $120 per month is feasible, off-setting the additional costs of using the CHPCs. There are over 93 million smallholder farmers in Nigeria, of which 70% are women, who will directly benefit from CHPCs as the technology as it rolls out across the country. ColdHubs believe there are opportunities to accelerate the adoption of this technology through licencing and franchising once the benefits are proven increasing the numbers benefitting. Jobs will be created as a result of the AAKTP both at ColdHubs and in the wider community. The company are pledged to recruit the AAKTP Associate at the conclusion of the project to develop an internal research and development capability.
